slidetranscripts.slidetranscript: <Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Welcome to the Butterfly Distribution Range Shift activity. This activity contains audio and will take about 15 minutes to complete. When you are ready to begin, you can select the next button at the bottom right of the player menu." /> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" LeadingMargin="0" TrailingMargin="0" FirstLineMargin="0" Justification="Left" LineSpacingRule="Multiple" LineSpacing="23" SpacingBefore="0" SpacingAfter="8"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="Now that you have observed a range change, you are going to compare the data for arrival and breeding opportunity of the butterflies." /> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" Justification="Left" LineSpacing="21" SpacingAfter="6"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="A climate model projects suitable summer conditions farther uphill. Both butterfly species have been recorded reaching the upper area, but repeated breeding has not yet been established. Assume adult nectar and other conditions are adequate during the periods described.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" Justification="Left" LineSpacing="21" SpacingAfter="6"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="Let’s look at the data:
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" Justification="Left" LineSpacing="21" SpacingAfter="6"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="The evidence we will be comparing between butterfly A and butterfly B is their dispersal and how many host plants are at the destination.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" Justification="Left" LineSpacing="21" SpacingAfter="6"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="Butterfly A is recorded to frequently cross the intervening landscape, while butterfly B crosses less frequently.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" Justification="Left" LineSpacing="21" SpacingAfter="6"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="Butterfly A encounters hosts that are widespread over the area, while butterfly B encounters hosts in several, small patches.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" Justification="Left" LineSpacing="21" SpacingAfter="6"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" Justification="Left" LineSpacing="21" SpacingAfter="6"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="Which butterfly appears more likely to expand its breeding range?
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" Justification="Left" LineSpacing="21" SpacingAfter="6"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="Select butterfly A or B. 
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" Justification="Left" LineSpacing="21" SpacingAfter="6"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" TrailingMargin="0" Justification="Left" LineSpacing="21" SpacingAfter="6"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="Let’s see if you prediction changes when we take a look at what was recorded regarding the butterflies timing." /> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" LeadingMargin="0" TrailingMargin="0" FirstLineMargin="0" Justification="Left" LineSpacingRule="Multiple" LineSpacing="23" SpacingBefore="0" SpacingAfter="8"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="For the last activity, you will predict more range responses and explain how it relates to the landscape.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" LeadingMargin="0" TrailingMargin="0" FirstLineMargin="0" Justification="Left" LineSpacingRule="Multiple" LineSpacing="23" SpacingBefore="0" SpacingAfter="8"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style FlowDirection="LeftToRight" LeadingMargin="0" TrailingMargin="0" FirstLineMargin="0" Justification="Left" LineSpacingRule="Multiple" LineSpacing="23" SpacingBefore="0" SpacingAfter="8"> <ListStyle ListType="None" ListTypeFormat="Parentheses" BulletFont="Arial" /> </Style> <Span Text="Your learning objective for Section 3 is to “Predict range responses using organismal traits and landscape connectivity, and defend an applied recommendation using a biological mechanism and evidence." /> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="New evidence and decision context: Butterfly B has enough time to complete its egg and larval period after arrival, but reaches the upper area less frequently. Additional observations identify long gaps between usable host and nectar patches along the intervening landscape. For this decision, assume improving those patches can facilitate movement and the restored plants can establish under projected conditions.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Conservation managers can fund one action to improveButterfly B’s opportunity to expand uphill.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Option 1: Add its larval host and adult nectar plants to several intervening patches, reducing gaps between usable patches.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Option 2: Increase nectar flowers at the destination, where adult nectar and the existing breeding resources are adequate for arriving individuals.
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="
" /> </Block> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Option 3: Increase the size of its existing lower-elevation habitat without improving the intervening landscape." /> </Block> </Content> </Document>

<Document xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"> <Content> <Block> <Style /> <Span Text="Great job! You have completed the butterfly migration activity. Next you will move on and use your new knowledge to complete the main assignment in Canvas. To view the answers you selected and typed during the activity, select the Review Saved Answers button." /> </Block> </Content> </Document>
